children: China's consumption likely is seeing an upgrade in demand among higher-income consumers despite overall spending, according to BofA Securities in a commentary. "The shift is most evident in everyday discretionary categories, where international brands are regaining share among affluent households in higher-tier cities," the bank says, citing its own survey. This is consistent with trends seen in cosmetics brands and may reflect "modestly improving" sentiment among middle-class and higher-income consumers, BofA says. The recovery is concentrated in daily consumption rather than luxury goods, the bank adds. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
